rationale: The design correctly implements route WORKSPACE→CONVERSATION→MESSAGE→REACTION with resolution_mode 'absent': the single seeded workspace's core-infra channel contains the exact content-identified root-cause message (1706001931.000000, Priya, CUDA memory limit) which has zero reactions in the base seed, so no workspace satisfies the full chain — consistent with 'absent'. The prompt's relationship phrasing ('channel named core-infra', 'the message where Priya pinned down...', 'that message got a check reaction') is faithfully translated into same-record binding requirements, explicitly called out in binding_note (channel/message/reaction must be the same triple). Negative roles are well-chosen plausible near-misses: (a) the root-cause message itself has no reaction, (b) a newly-added check reaction sits on a different message in the same correct channel (a genuine same-channel/wrong-message distractor), and (c) an existing 'eyes' reaction sits on a different message/channel entirely. The added check-reaction record is a legitimate design-stage mutation (not yet in base seed, to be added by the compiler) and does not alter any existing intended referents. 'check' is within the documented reaction-write vocabulary. The access plan (conversations.list/users.conversations → conversations.history → reactions.get) uses only real, documented API operations, on a public channel, requiring no unsupported capability or hidden-ID assumption. Answer_attributes (teams.team_id/team_name) are real bare columns, and since the seed contains exactly one workspace, the answer resolves cleanly to 'no qualifying workspace' without requiring an unsupported workspace-name-lookup call. Quality is strong: concise realistic wording, a consequential-feeling verification question, and useful same-channel/wrong-message and wrong-channel/wrong-emoji negatives that don't leak the answer.
